restated_task: Add an instance method `Version.is_compatible(other: Version) -> bool` to the Version class in src/semver/version.py. The method returns True when `other` (the new version) can be used in place of `self` (the old version). Compatibility rules: majors must be equal; new.minor >= old.minor; prerelease parts must be equal (both None counts as equal); patch is ignored. Major version 0 is special: only identical versions (major, minor, patch, prerelease all equal) are compatible. If `other` is not a Version instance (subclasses allowed), raise TypeError with message starting with 'Expected a Version type but got ' followed by the type representation. Add a docstring with at least two doctest examples. Do not modify any other public behavior, tests, docs, or packaging; keep the existing pytest suite passing.

interface_contract.name: Version.is_compatible
interface_contract.behavior: Returns True when `other` (new version) can replace `self` (old version) per semantic versioning compatibility rules: majors equal; other.minor >= self.minor; prerelease parts equal (both None counts as equal); patch ignored. Major version 0 is special: only identical versions (major, minor, patch, prerelease all equal) are compatible. Subclasses of Version are accepted as `other`.
error_cases: TypeError: raised when `other` is not an instance of Version (or subclass); message must start with 'Expected a Version type but got ' followed by the type representation (e.g., "<class 'str'>").

acceptance_criteria: Version(0, 1, 0).is_compatible(Version(0, 1, 1)) is False (major 0 requires identical patch)

Version(1, 2, 3).is_compatible({'a': 2}) raises TypeError with message starting with 'Expected a Version type but got <class 'dict'>'
Version(1, 2, 3).is_compatible([]) raises TypeError with message starting with 'Expected a Version type but got <class 'list'>'
class CustomVersion(Version): pass; CustomVersion(1, 0, 0).is_compatible(Version(1, 0, 0)) is True (subclass accepted)
